transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Celestia Head of Security), Omar (Cloud Architect), Sofia (Compliance), Jon (Infra)

Auto-summary: Quick workshop to align on SAML/SCIM onboarding and RBAC/least-privilege patterns, plus detailed questions around KMS and audit logs for an upcoming pilot.

00:00 Ethan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. Quick round robin then we'll jump into the KMS and SAML items.
00:20 Marta: Hi, Marta here. We'll probably ask a lot of scoping questions - trying to map to our compliance checklist.
00:30 Omar: Hey, Omar, we'll be looking at the VPC and keyflow side primarily.
00:36 Priya: Great, thanks. I can share configuration examples as we go; I'll drop SAML metadata and SCIM mapping later.
01:05 Sofia: Quick note - timeline is tight; internal audit is late May so we want to have the pilot and logs in place by mid-May ideally.
01:30 Ethan: Noted. We'll aim to surface the SOC2 items first. Priya, do you want to kick off on SSO?
01:45 Priya: Sure. High level - Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM 2.0 for user provisioning. For SAML we can ingest IdP metadata, and map attributes to Redwood roles. SCIM allows us to sync groups and membership. Typical pitfalls: attribute naming and group scoping.
02:20 Omar: For attribute naming, are you expecting eduPerson style or custom claims?
02:33 Priya: We can accept both. Common attributes we map: email, given_name, family_name, and a group claim for role mapping. If customers use custom claims we include a small mapping layer in the console.
02:50 Marta: How do you handle Just-in-time provisioning vs full SCIM provisioning? We prefer SCIM for auditability but JIT is tempting.
03:05 Priya: SCIM is recommended for enterprise - it's auditable and allows deprovisioning. JIT works for bootsrapped teams but it's harder to guarantee least-privilege.
03:28 Jon: For RBAC, we want to avoid too many broad admin roles. Can we do role hierarchies and role slices?
03:45 Priya: Yes, Redwood supports role templates and custom roles. You can create scopes: organization-wide admin, project-level operator, observer, billing. We also recommend using least-privilege by default and a small set of break-glass accounts.
04:20 Sofia: Are role changes logged? We need to show who changed role bindings for SOC evidence.
04:32 Priya: Role changes are auditable. We log actor, timestamp, old/new role, and that's exportable via the audit logs API.
05:00 Ethan: On to encryption - Marta I know you had specific KMS questions?
05:15 Marta: Yeah, specifically, can Redwood integrate with our Cloud KMS and optionally bring HSM-backed keys?
05:28 Priya: Two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed keys where Redwood holds the master key and we do envelope encryption and rotate keys regularly; 2) BYOK (bring your own key) where you supply a KMS key (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and we perform envelope encryption with that root. We also support external HSMs via customer KMS connectors for private deployments.
06:10 Omar: If we do BYOK, do you ever see plaintext model context? We need to ensure keys are never exported and data at rest is encrypted in our tenant region.
06:28 Priya: With BYOK + private deployment, keys are never exported. The envelope flow ensures plaintext is only in-memory on the inference host and protected by disk encryption. We can provide a threat model doc.
06:52 Marta: What about key rotation and revocation? Audit and proof we can revoke access quickly.
07:05 Priya: We support key rotation and we surface rotation events in audit logs. If you revoke a KMS key, new tokens can't be decrypted — you have to rewrap. We have a documented migration pattern for rewrapping data.
07:30 Jon: For pilot we'd like to try a small dataset and validate end-to-end without touching production keys. Is there a sandbox for BYOK?
07:45 Priya: Yes, we can do a sandbox flow. For hosted customers we offer a sandbox keys flow and for private deployments we can run a trial with your test KMS key in a dedicated VPC.
08:12 Sofia: Data residency - our regs require logs and tokens to be stored in EU-only region. Can you guarantee that?
08:26 Ethan: Redwood has region controls and private deployments can be constrained to a region. For hosted we have region selection; for strict residency we recommend private deployment or dedicated capacity in the EU region.
08:50 Omar: For audit logs, we plan to push logs to our SIEM. Is there a push/export mechanism?
09:00 Priya: Logs are exportable. We have native S3 export and syslog/HTTP webhook sinks to forward to SIEM, and also a streaming export to major cloud logging endpoints.
09:20 Marta: Retention policy - can we set custom retention per tenant?
09:28 Priya: Yes, retention is configurable; default retention is 90 days for hostings but for enterprise customers we can configure long-term retention or integrate with your archival store.
09:45 Sofia: For SOC 2 evidence — do you provide controls mapping and a gap analysis?
09:53 Ethan: We provide a SOC2 summary, and for deeper work we can provide control mappings and sample evidence packages. I'll send the Type II report and a compliance FAQ after this call.
10:20 Marta: Regarding SCIM group sync - what if group cardinality is huge? We have thousands of groups in some tenants.
10:35 Priya: We recommend scoping: sync only relevant groups, or use a prefix-based filter. We also support incremental SCIM syncs rather than full syncs.
11:00 Omar: A subtle question - what happens if SCIM membership syncs are delayed and someone is still in access? Do you have TTLs or session invalidation?
11:18 Priya: We support session invalidation hooks and a short cache TTL for group membership so revocations take effect within a configured window (configurable down to a few minutes for critical roles).
11:45 Jon: For SAML we need an example of NameID, group claim and role mapping.
11:55 Priya: I'll share a sample SAML metadata file and an attribute mapping table after the call.
12:10 Marta: On-boarding flow - what admin approvals are required? Can we limit who can authorize provisioning?
12:25 Priya: Yes, onboarding requires an owner to accept the SAML trust and one or two admin confirmations depending on the org policy. You can require an approvals workflow for SCIM provisioning.
12:50 Sofia: We're concerned about privileged accounts. Do you have recommendations for break-glass and emergency access audits?
13:05 Priya: Recommended pattern: create a small set of break-glass accounts with MFA and TTL-limited sessions, require multi-person approvals for sensitive actions, and log all break-glass usage separately. We also recommend periodic role recertification.
13:40 Ethan: Switching back to KMS - Priya you mentioned HSM connectors for private deployments. Can you elaborate on the integration modes?
13:55 Priya: Sure. For private deployments we support two integration modes: direct KMS API where the customer KMS (with HSM backing) does the master key ops, and an HSM agent model where an on-prem HSM is proxied into the Redwood control plane via an encrypted tunnel. The latter is for air-gapped or highly regulated setups.
14:34 Omar: Latency concerns - if KMS operations are synchronous on every request, that will add latency. How do you mitigate?
14:46 Priya: We use envelope encryption and cache the data encryption keys (DEKs) in memory with TTL to avoid frequent master key calls. Master key ops occur mainly on key rotation or when creating new DEKs.
15:10 Marta: Is there a risk that an attacker with host access could extract DEKs from memory?
15:20 Priya: We harden the host: memory protections, page-locking for key material when possible, and minimal privilege runtimes. For the highest assurance we recommend HSM-backed private deployment and more restrictive host-level controls.
15:52 Jon: For SIEM integration, what fields are available in the logs? We need actor id, action, resource, result, and geo/region.
16:05 Priya: Logs include actor email/id, role, ip, action, resource id, result code, timestamp, and optionally request/response duration. We can also add custom context fields if needed.
16:32 Sofia: Does Redwood retain PII in logs? We need to avoid adding full tokens or sensitive payloads.
16:42 Priya: By default we redact PII in logs; full request bodies are only retained when explicitly enabled for debugging and then must be approved and time-limited.
17:02 Ethan: Competition question - some vendors force customers to hand over key material or don't provide HSM patterns. Did you compare to BigComputeAI?
17:15 Marta: Yes, we've seen smaller vendors with limited BYOK.
17:22 Priya: Redwood's differentiator is flexible key patterns and private deployment for strict reg requirements.
17:40 Omar: Cost tradeoffs - HSM-backed private deployment will raise costs. We need a rough TCO estimate vs managed keys.
17:52 Ethan: I'll include a TCO note in the follow-up doc. For pilot, use hosted with BYOK sandbox, then evaluate private HSM if necessary.
18:18 Jon: We also need to test role change propagation and the revocation timeline in a staging run.
18:28 Priya: We can run a role-propagation test during the pilot and capture end-to-end logs.
18:50 Marta: For evidence for auditors, can you timestamp proof of key rotation events and who initiated them?
19:00 Priya: Yes, rotation events are logged with the initiator id, request origin, and version ID.
19:20 Sofia: Are there any known limitations or gaps for SOC controls?
19:30 Ethan: For full SOC support we have documented controls; there may be specific customer evidence requests that require additional instrumentation — we'll do a gap analysis if needed.
19:50 Omar: About SCIM mapping - our directory sends groups as nested JSON sometimes. Does Redwood's SCIM parser handle nested groups?
20:05 Priya: We handle flat group lists natively; for nested groups we can flatten on our side or we recommend sending an expanded group claim. We can share transform scripts.
20:40 Jon: Session recording — do you support session replay or screen capture? Our auditors asked about devops session recordings.
20:50 Priya: We don't provide full session replay as part of standard product; we integrate with session recording tools via audit hooks, though.
21:15 Marta: Another compliance point - how do you handle data deletion requests?
21:25 Priya: We support tenant-level deletion flags and can purge customer data per policy. For backups/archives we have documented erase/rewrite flows. We'll include the deletion SLA in the follow-up.
21:50 Ethan: Ok, quick recap and gaps: we need to share SOC2/ISO docs, SAML metadata and SCIM mapping templates, a sample RBAC matrix, and a KMS integration whitepaper. Anything else?
22:10 Sofia: Also include the retention config examples and log export formats.
22:18 Priya: Noted. We'll also prepare a small runbook for key rotation and compromise scenarios.
22:35 Omar: On the pilot plan, can we do a two-week sandbox test with BYOK and group sync?
22:42 Priya: Yes, two-week sandbox is fine. We'll need a test KMS key and a scoped set of users.
23:00 Jon: Last question - do you support SAML multiple IdPs per tenant for orgs with federated subsidiaries?
23:10 Priya: Yes, we support multiple IdP bindings per org and per project-level overrides.
23:30 Marta: Cool. That's helpful. Thanks everyone.
23:40 Ethan: Great. We'll capture all action items and send over the documents. Thanks for the time.

Post-call notes:
- Priya to attach SAML metadata sample and SCIM mapping with group prefix examples.
- Team to validate retention and SIEM export format with Jon's sample logs.
- Plan BD/AE follow-up for pilot pricing and TCO.

End of transcript.
